item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption provides advice on corruption risks during public sector mergers and restructures.
item.support: The aim of this report is to alert public sector managers to the corruption pitfalls during and following organisational change

item.text: It examines how large organisational changes affect controls, incentives and opportunities for misconduct, using investigation case studies.
item.support: It explores why and how large-scale organisational change initiatives create opportunities for corruption

item.text: The Commission concludes that poorly managed change can create corruption opportunities through inadequate processes or unrecognised shifts in incentives.
item.support: These opportunities can arise from poorly designed, conflicting or inadequate processes

item.text: The Commission advises agencies to build continuing change-management capacity, conduct early due diligence, strengthen high-risk controls and monitor progress against planned milestones.
item.support: Organisations that have developed a standing change management capability are better placed to manage these challenges.

item.quote: If not managed well, organisational change can provide opportunities for corruption.
